items.sentence: The NHS says metoclopramide is usually taken for a short time.
MedlinePlus, a US source, also describes its use for slowed stomach emptying and for reflux symptoms.
StatPearls describes metoclopramide as a dopamine-2 receptor antagonist that is mainly used as an anti-sickness medicine.

In the basal ganglia, the brain area that helps control movement, blocking dopamine receptors upsets the balance between dopamine and acetylcholine, which is the proposed route to its movement side effects.
These movement effects include sudden muscle spasms (acute dystonia), restlessness (akathisia), parkinsonism and tardive dyskinesia.
Drowsiness, low mood or depression, and diarrhoea are the most frequently listed common side effects, according to the NHS.
Uncontrollable movements such as tics, tremors, muscle stiffness and spasms
MedlinePlus, a US source, says tardive dyskinesia, a movement disorder, may not go away after metoclopramide is stopped, and that the risk rises the longer treatment lasts.
MedlinePlus also says older adults should not usually take metoclopramide for those uses.
The NHS lists seizures as a reason to call 999 or go to A&E.
The NHS says alcohol will make a person feel more sleepy.
StatPearls describes neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a rare life-threatening reaction, as a possible complication of metoclopramide; it needs emergency care by calling 999.
